# Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta (MN 123 (PTS MN iii 118))

**ID:** MN 123 (PTS MN iii 118)

**Title (Pali):** Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Incredible and Amazing

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta* (MN 123; PTS MN iii 118) is a discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya* of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In this text, the Venerable Ānanda is invited by the Buddha to speak on the Buddha’s marvellous and extraordinary qualities (*acchariya-abbhuta-dhamma*), and Ānanda recounts a sequence of miraculous occurrences surrounding the Bodhisatta's descent from the Tusita heaven, his stay in his mother's womb, and his birth [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2011; Sujato 2012a]. The discourse culminates with the Buddha clarifying what he considers truly amazing about himself, including the mindful rising, persisting, and ending of feelings, perceptions, and thoughts [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2012a]. As an exemplar of the canonical *abbhūtadhamma* genre (*aṅga*), it reflects devotional and biographical developments regarding the Bodhisatta [Norman 1983; Sujato 2012b]. Modern scholars note that Ānanda's list appears to expand upon the account of Buddha Vipassī found in the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), adapting those mythic marvels into the life story of Gotama Buddha [Norman 1983; Sujato 2011; Sujato 2012a]. Moreover, the extensive variations across canonical recensions suggest that elements were added over time during its transmission [Sujato & Brahmali 2015; Anālayo 2014].

Curated parallels include the Chinese Madhyama-āgama discourse MĀ 32 and the Pali *Catukkanipāta* discourse AN 4.127 [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2014]. DharmaNexus confirms substantial text reuse within the Pali canon, notably sharing 161 matching passages (19,418 characters) with the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), 86 matches with AN 4, as well as connections with the *Bākula Sutta* (MN 124), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and various Saṁyutta discourses [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies textual alignments in Chinese (notably the *Dīrghāgama*, T 1, and the *Seven Buddhas Sūtra*, T 2), Sanskrit parallels (such as the *Mahāvadānasūtra*, *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*), and Tibetan parallels (including the *Abhiniṣkramaṇasūtra*, D 301) [DharmaNexus].
